source_lines.34: **Assume the axiom of choice** ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a chosen $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module that is integrable, has finite-dimensional label-weight spaces and weight set contained in a finite union of cones $\lambda-Q_+$ ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]).
source_lines.36: (i) **Splitting along the top isotypic part.** Let $\lambda$ be a maximal weight of $M$, put $N_0:=U_q(\mathfrak g)M_\lambda$ and let $N_1$ be the sum of the remaining simple constituents, so that $M=N_0\oplus N_1$ and $N_0\cong V(\lambda)^{\oplus m}$ with $m=\dim M_\lambda$. Then $L=(L\cap N_0)\oplus(L\cap N_1)$, $B=\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_0)/q(L\cap N_0)\bigr)\sqcup\bigl(B\cap(L\cap N_1)/q(L\cap N_1)\bigr)$, and both pairs are crystal bases of $N_0$ and $N_1$.
source_lines.38: (ii) **Uniqueness.** There is a locally weight-finite indexed family $(\lambda_j)_{j\in J}$ in $P^+$ and an isomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules $\Phi:M\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\bigoplus_{j\in J}V(\lambda_j)$ with $\Phi(L)=\bigoplus_j\mathcal L(\lambda_j)$ and $\Phi$ inducing a bijection $B\to\bigsqcup_j\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ of crystals. The multiset $\{\lambda_j:j\in J\}$ is the multiset of highest weights of the simple integrable constituents of $M$: the number of $j$ with $\lambda_j=\lambda$ equals the multiplicity $[M:V(\lambda)]$.
source_lines.40: (iii) **Components.** Through $\Phi$ the connected components of the crystal $B$ are exactly the canonical highest weight crystals $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$; each component has a unique highest weight element $b$, of dominant weight $\lambda$, and equals the lowering-generated subcrystal $F(b)$ of [[def-highest-weight-element-and-connected-highest-weight-crystal]]. In particular the crystal graph of any crystal basis of $M$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$, and no other highest weight elements occur.

source_lines.78: 7.1 Step H: components. Under $\Phi$ the connected components of $B$ are exactly the $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$: each $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ is connected because by [F4] every vertex is a lowering word from $b_{\lambda_j}$, and distinct copies share no vertices, so the partition into copies is the partition into connected components. Each $\mathcal B(\lambda_j)$ has highest weight element $b_{\lambda_j}$ of dominant weight $\lambda_j$ and equals $F(b_{\lambda_j})$ by [F5], and it has no other highest weight element by the uniqueness clause of [F5]; hence the highest weight elements of $B$ are exactly the $b_{\lambda_j}$, each generating its own component, and the crystal graph of $B$ is determined up to isomorphism by $M$. source_lines.70: 2.1 The mixed commutators. For $i\ne j$, use the genuine finite-wedge module of [[thm-normally-ordered-q-wedges-form-a-basis]], obtained from the vector module by the coproduct of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] and a quantum-group-stable kernel. Its operators satisfy $[E_i^{[N]},F_j^{[N]}]=0$, where $[N]$ denotes the prefix length, not a divided power. For a given partition choose $N$ beyond the nonvacuum rows of that partition and all its finitely many one- and two-step node outputs. The stable-prefix formula gives $F_j=F_j^{[N]}$ after tail attachment and $E_i=q^{-\delta_{i\equiv -N}}E_i^{[N]}$ after tail attachment, with the same scalar on both intermediate diagrams. Thus $[E_i,F_j]$ is the image of $q^{-\delta_{i\equiv -N}}[E_i^{[N]},F_j^{[N]}]$ and is zero. No relation for the infinite module is assumed in this finite calculation. For $i=j$, the exact tensor cubes in [F2] give $[E_i,F_i]=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q-q^{-1})$. [step 1.1, F1, F2, given, algebra]
